title: Bidirectional A* in Belém: find the fastest route!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* race from start and goal toward each other, dramatically reducing the search space. Using a grid/graph derived from real streets, it blends heuristic guidance with two-front expansion for faster convergence.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ **Bidirectional A*** is doing the sprint in **Belém’s street graph**—starting simultaneously from both the origin and destination. 

🔍 In graph terms, we treat streets/intersections as a weighted graph and run two coordinated A* searches: one forward, one backward. ✅ Each frontier uses an admissible heuristic (think: lower-bound distance), so expansions stay directed—then the moment the frontiers meet, the algorithm stitches the optimal path together. 

📍 This visualization mirrors how route planners compress reality: real map segments become nodes/edges, weights reflect travel costs, and the heuristic prunes detours early. 

🎥 Want your city next? Comment a district + challenge (e.g., “avoid hills” or “minimize turns”) and I’ll generate the map graph + visualization for it! 💬
fb_caption:
Ever wonder how route-finding finds the *best* path without checking every street? 🚗💡 **Bidirectional A*** searches from both the start and the goal at the same time, using heuristics to expand smarter and meet in the middle—so the optimal path is found with far fewer explored nodes. 

📌 Like this post if you want more algorithm visualizations, and share a city/district for the next real-map test!
yt_description:
